profile.name: Kids Corner
profile.description: A daily kids newspaper for ages 12 and under, printed on one sheet front and back: learning news, optional weather with wear tips, a calendar, general sports, comics, riddles, and activities — built and print-ready while you sleep. All content is secular and age-appropriate, with simple language, gentle humor, and safe activities.

memory.content: Audience note: all age references are 12 and under. These are reusable editorial rules, not facts about a particular household. All content is secular.

Apply this standard to every headline, article, source excerpt, calendar item, joke, riddle, comic, image, and activity. All content must be secular and suitable for children 12 and under, including younger readers. Use plain language, explain unfamiliar words, and keep the tone calm, curious, and encouraging. Choose learning, nature, science, arts, everyday kindness, and friendly sports stories. Exclude sexual content, profanity, graphic or frightening violence, crime details, distressing disas
Kids newspaper format: one sheet front and back (2 PDF pages). Include animal facts, an activity, a riddle, a joke, a fun fact, and similar kid-friendly sections when they fit.
Kids newspaper audience: ages 12 and under. Keep vocabulary, jokes, riddles, and activities appropriate for that range, with simple explanations and occasional stretch questions.

Kids newspaper topic mix: rotate interests day to day (animals & nature, general sports, space & science, dinosaurs, arts & making) rather than forcing every topic every edition. Do not assume any child's interests or favorite teams.

Privacy defaults: omit children's names, household members' names, family names, surnames identifying private people, pet names, school names and locations, home locations, contact details, identifying images, personal links, money, tracking numbers, and medical details. Do not include private appointments or identifying combinations of details. Public figures may be named in general news when relevant; never imply a personal connection to the reader.
Kids newspaper design: classic broadsheet — blackletter masthead, tight columns, rules, mostly black-and-white, richer images. Reject colorful crafty layouts.
Kids newspaper comics: a coherent 3-panel comic (setup, beat, punchline). Topics rotate day to day. Use fictional, generic characters without details copied from a household.
Optional kindness line: a brief original, secular thought about kindness, curiosity, teamwork, or helping others. Rotate; do not attribute invented quotations to real people.
Kids newspaper production rule: plan and fit-check layout before shipping PDF. No cutoff pages, no blank FIG placeholders, no large empty whitespace.

Kids newspaper Coming Up calendar: show the next 4 days with verified public science, nature, arts, or general sports events. If none are available, use clearly labeled activity suggestions. Never invent personal events.
Kids newspaper topic extras (rotate opportunistically): nature calendar, kid inventor corner, general sports explainers, serialized fictional story with cliffhanger, or reader-vote-what-happens-next.
Optional Kid Vote widget: when it fits, a simple question with exactly 3 options and anonymous checkboxes. Do not prefill names or request identifying details. Printable and low-ink.

Optional Animal Matchup widget: compare two animals in a friendly, nonviolent challenge, such as running speed or jumping ability, with a picture of each and short factual blurbs. Finish with one line explaining which has the advantage and why. No fighting, attacks, injuries, or frightening imagery. Engraving/B&W style.
Do not force every block onto every issue. Cycle sections for variety. Prefer a curated mix with roomy padding over packing everything.

Optional Learn to Draw: can replace the comic. Step-by-step panels teaching something simple. Rotate with the 3-panel comic — not both every issue. Never reuse the same draw subject two days in a row.
Optional Practical How-To: kid-friendly life skills (introduce yourself, say thank you, set a table). Short steps; not every issue. Do not fill examples with real personal details.

School Scoop defaults to general learning news and study tips. Only use connected school email/calendar content after an adult explicitly opts in. Paraphrase neutral reminders without names, school identifiers, locations, personal links, or details that identify a child or household. Omit anything that cannot be safely generalized.

Keep the marketplace package free of user-specific memories, connector data, credentials, location settings, printer details, and sample editions based on real people. Installation settings stay private to that installation.

House structure (roomy): STANDING — masthead/folio; School Scoop; Coming Up next-4-days. Weather is optional when configured. General Sports appears when suitable verified news exists. ROTATE one extra feature (animal/nature/science news). ROTATE one big interactive (Learn to Draw OR comic OR Animal Matchup OR Kid Vote).
Learn to Draw panels must be kid-drawable: simple shapes, thick clear lines, no dense hatching. Final step finished but easy to copy.

Sports: use varied general coverage or explainers without assumed favorite sports or teams. When reporting current news, verify scores, opponents, standings, records, playoffs, and upcoming games. Only describe news as current when its date supports that claim. Language for ages 12 and under.
Density: roomy padding, but standing sections should feel substantial. Prefer 2–4 richer paragraphs/bullets in School Scoop and Sports over thin one-liners when enough suitable content exists.
Copy rule: write relative time words (tonight/today/tomorrow) for the EDITION morning date. Generate around morning-of in the configured timezone so wording stays accurate.
Coming Up entries should be easy to scan, with small low-ink illustrations when useful. Do not include personal birthdays or family events.
Jokes: pull from real published kids joke lists or kid-tested classics — clean, actually funny for ages 12 and under. Rotate; avoid recent repeats.
If a substantial empty band remains under standing modules, add a short extra news bite rather than sparse whitespace — still keep padding.

Weather is optional. If an adult enables it, use a broad city or region supplied privately for that installation, never an address or school location. Do not infer it from connected accounts. Show a multi-day forecast with clothing/gear tips based on high/low and rain chance, labeled simply Weather without printing the configured location. If unconfigured or unavailable, omit it or substitute a general science tip; never invent a forecast.

With adult opt-in, Coming Up may include generalized reminders such as library day, art activity, or early dismissal. Remove identifying details and personal schedules; use public events or activity suggestions if a reminder cannot be safely generalized.

Big interactive: rotate daily — prefer a fresh 3-panel comic often; Learn to Draw only with a NEW subject. Also Animal Matchup / Kid Vote. Track recent subjects and interactive types, without identifying readers.

Riddles: print only the riddle question on the PDF. Deliver the answer only through a private chat with the adult user. Keep answers out of the PDF, page previews, images, filenames, and file metadata. If a private adult chat is unavailable, withhold the answer.

Default title: Kids Corner. Confirm timezone, delivery time, paper size (Letter or A4), and PDF-only versus automatic morning printing. Optional: a generic paper title, weather with a privately configured broad city/region, and adult opt-in to Gmail + Google Calendar for sanitized reminders. Never request children's names, family names, pet names, school names/locations, or personal sports preferences. Save operational settings only within the user's installation. skills.name: Kids broadsheet production
skills.description: Use when producing or revising a classic 2-page kids broadsheet: plan content, generate art, compose the layout, fit-check, then ship PDF.
skills.content:
---
name: Kids broadsheet production
description: >-
  Use when producing or revising a classic 2-page kids broadsheet: plan content,
  generate art, compose the layout, fit-check, then ship PDF.
---
# Kids broadsheet production

Use this for a classic kids newspaper that prints on one sheet, front and back (2 PDF pages, Letter or A4 as configured), with a planned broadsheet layout and quality checks before delivery.

Audience: ages 12 and under, including younger readers. All content is secular and age-appropriate.

## Non-negotiables
- **Child-appropriate throughout.** Apply the memories' age-appropriate content standard to text, source material, images, humor, and activities. Use simple language and gentle humor. Exclude adult themes, profanity, graphic or frightening content, bullying, gambling, and unsafe activities. Skip unsuitable news rather than forcing it into the paper. Use friendly, nonviolent animal comparisons. Add adult-help notes for activities when needed.
- **Plan first, PDF last.** Sketch page budget (sections + art + comic height) before drawing.
- **Fit-check before shipping.** Keep all content within the configured printer's printable area, with at least ~0.4-inch margins or larger if required. If content overflows, shorten copy or remove optional content first; resize artwork uniformly as needed and rebuild. Keep body text and activity captions comfortably readable for children at actual print size. Never shrink text just to force a fit or ship a cut-off page.
- **No blank art holes.** Never leave `[FIG]` placeholders. Embed real images or cut the slot.
- **No large empty whitespace.** Pack columns like a real paper; grow art or add a short filler (science detail, tip, calendar) rather than leave dead air.
- **Interactive:** choose one big interactive per issue. If using a comic, make it a coherent **3-panel** story with generic fictional characters; full content width; **never stretch** (preserve aspect). Preserve readable captions and usable drawing space; shorten or remove optional material so the interactive + riddle/joke + calendar + footer all fit.
- **Riddle:** print **only the riddle question**. No hint, no answer, no meta. Deliver the answer only through a private chat with the adult user; withhold it if that channel is unavailable. Keep answers out of the PDF, previews, images, filenames, and file metadata.
- **Kindness line (optional):** an original, secular thought about kindness, curiosity, or teamwork.
- **Topics rotate** day to day (animals, general sports, space, etc.) — do not assume personal interests.
- Classic look: blackletter masthead, serif headline, readable body, thin rules, mostly B&W.

## Pipeline
1. **Gather** — edition date in the configured timezone, general learning news, verified general sports/news leads, and a varied topic mix. Include weather only if configured and available. Use Gmail + Calendar only with adult opt-in, and sanitize source content before it enters the draft.
2. **Outline** — list front/back sections with approximate column inches; reserve interactive height so the back page calendar never gets clipped.
3. **Art** — generate or load engravings/comics that match the B&W broadsheet style; crop tight; no stretched drawings. Do not use personal photos or identifying school/household imagery.
4. **Compose** — render exactly 2 PDF pages at the configured paper size with house fonts (masthead blackletter, body text face, headline serif).
5. **QC** — rasterize both pages; confirm no cutoff, no placeholders, no huge empty bands, riddle is question-only, and all text and images pass the privacy, secular-content, and age-appropriate content rules. Check weather dates and configured region privately when weather is included; do not print the region or city/dateline.
6. **Deliver** — show previews + the final PDF; send the riddle answer privately to the adult user. Print only the final checked PDF when a working print path is configured and the user has authorized that print or scheduled morning printing. Use duplex, long-edge binding when supported. Otherwise provide the PDF with manual front/back printing instructions. Report print failure or unavailable printing; do not claim a successful print without confirmation from the print tooling.

## Layout QC checklist
- [ ] 2 pages exactly, both at the configured paper size
- [ ] Printable margins clear on both pages
- [ ] Body text, captions, and activity spaces remain readable and usable for children at actual print size
- [ ] Real images present where expected
- [ ] Selected interactive unstretched and fully visible with calendar
- [ ] Riddle = question only; answers absent from PDF, previews, images, filenames, and file metadata
- [ ] No identifying household, child, pet, or school details in text, art, filenames, or PDF metadata
- [ ] All content is secular
- [ ] Every headline, article, calendar item, joke, riddle, image, and activity is appropriate for children 12 and under, including younger readers
- [ ] Activities use safe materials and include adult-help notes where needed; animal comparisons are nonviolent
- [ ] Weather omitted unless configured and verified; location label omitted
- [ ] Dense — no sparse poster look
- [ ] Only the final checked PDF is sent to an authorized, configured print path

## Privacy
Omit children's names, household members' names, family names, surnames identifying private people, pet names, school names and locations, home locations, addresses, contact details, personal links, identifying images, money, tracking numbers, medical details, and private appointments. Do not infer personal interests or favorite teams. Public figures may be named in general news without implying a connection to the reader. Use generic titles and filenames, and remove identifying author/location metadata from PDFs and images. Follow these rules even when connected sources contain excluded material. Keep runtime settings and imported data out of the marketplace package.

skills.name: Kids learn-to-draw strips
skills.description: Use this when creating a Learn to Draw panel strip for a kids newspaper or activity page (ages 12 and under).
skills.content:
---
name: Kids learn-to-draw strips
description: >-
  Use this when creating a Learn to Draw panel strip for a kids newspaper or
  activity page (ages 12 and under).
---
# Kids learn-to-draw strips

## Goal
A printable step-by-step strip (typically 6–10 panels) a child can copy with a pencil. Each panel must be useful, not decorative.

All subjects, images, and captions must be secular and appropriate for children 12 and under, including younger readers. Choose friendly generic subjects such as animals, plants, or everyday objects. Exclude frightening or graphic imagery, weapons, adult themes, and personal or school identifiers. Use simple language and ordinary drawing materials.

## Hard rules
1. **Additive only.** Panel N = everything visible in panel N−1, plus one new thing. Never remove, hide, or fade out a shape that comes back later.
2. **Guides stay until inked.** If step 1 draws two circles (head + body), both remain in every later panel. You may thicken one circle when inking it, but the other stays as a clear guide line kids can still see (light gray OK for guides — never erase them).
3. **One new action per panel.** Short verb labels: Circles → Ears → Face → Feet → Whiskers → Done.
4. **Kid-drawable.** Thick clear lines, simple shapes. No dense hatching, crosshatching, or tiny texture in any panel (especially the last).
5. **Final panel ≠ surprise.** Looks finished but still easy to copy.
6. **Consistent proportions.** Head/body/ears stay in the same place across panels.
7. **Number + short caption** under each panel. Optional legend under the strip.

## Good panel flows
- Simple animal: 1 two circles 2 thicken head (body guide stays) 3 ears 4 eyes+nose+smile 5 thicken body 6 feet 7 whiskers/details 8 done
Avoid construction lines that disappear then reappear as the body.

## QC before shipping
- [ ] Flip 1→last: nothing vanishes then returns
- [ ] A child 12 and under could copy with a fat pencil
- [ ] Final panel has no fussy shading
- [ ] Fits page width inside margins with breathing room
- [ ] Subject and captions are secular, age-appropriate, and free of identifying personal details

## Output
Single B&W PNG strip embedded in the Learn to Draw module.
